Mixed-vintage Senate snapshot: only MS-SEN refreshed. The other 34 rows retain November 4 vote/call data and evidence. snapshot_timestamp denotes the assembled component, not a new capture for every row.
MS-SEN DDHQ call is November 11 at 18:28 EST; displayed vote update November 12 at 12:24 EST. Minute-precision timestamps use zero seconds.
MS reporting is displayed as >95%; numeric percent_reporting withheld to avoid asserting an exact estimate. Vote shares remain incomplete and ineligible for share scoring.
House control uses explicit DDHQ chamber projection, not reconstructed district-threshold evidence. House counts remain preliminary: 255 D / 168 R / 12 undecided.
RCP national shares are 55.9% D and 42.7% R at displayed 93% reporting; observed November 12, source clock time unavailable. National vote scoring and final seat errors remain unavailable.
Frozen Kalshi volume confirmed USD by project owner November 9; original captured volume field remains unidentified.
approved_exceptions: DDHQ district threshold of 218 may establish House control with evidence.

figures.title: The Toss-Ups Separated the Forecasts
figures.subtitle: The differences in their overall records came from Toss-Ups and forecasts without a favorite.

figures.title: Every Source Expected Fewer Non-Republican Wins
figures.subtitle: Bars sum each source's win probabilities across the same 34 resolved races; the yellow line marks 21 actual wins.

figures.title: Scott Colom Was Every Source's Biggest Surprise
figures.subtitle: Each percentage is the chance a source gave the eventual winner; lower means a bigger surprise.

figures.title: Kalshi Consistently Gave Non-Republican Candidates Higher Odds
figures.subtitle: Five largest gaps versus the equal-weight Economist–VoteHub average; positive gaps mean higher odds.

figures.title: The Largest Kalshi–VoteHub Disagreements
figures.subtitle: Kalshi was closer to the called outcome in four of these five races; Louisiana favored VoteHub.

figures.subtitle: Kalshi was closer to the called outcome in four of these five races; Nebraska favored The Economist.

figures.title: House Control Offered Little Separation Between Sources

figures.title: Democrats Won Two Races Cook Favored Republicans to Win
